- When sentiment is strongly positive (≥ 0.5) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 2–5% for next period.
- When sentiment is strongly negative (≤ -0.5), model underestimates; adjust upward by 2–5% to account for risk reversal or panic-driven rebounds.
- Model consistently overreacts to recent price spikes (e.g., +10%+ in 3–5 days) — cap forecast increase after spike to avoid overshoot.
- Mean reversion bias: if 3–5 consecutive days show downward trend, model often fails to reverse; add 1–3% upward bias to counteract lagged mean reversion.
- For 30-day horizon, model underestimates true price volatility in early periods — increase forecast by 1–3% for first 7–10 days if sentiment is neutral or mildly positive.
- If sentiment history shows alternating highs/lows (e.g., +0.4, -1.2, +0.3), model tends to misalign with sentiment cycles — align forecast slope with sentiment trend direction, not just magnitude.
